summary: US-020: Publish a seat map — a seated slot coexists with GA
description:
### US-020: Publish a seat map — a seated slot coexists with GA
**As** an organizer, **I want** to publish a seat map and offer a performance as seated, **so that** downstream epics can claim seats (TKT-80) and buyers can pick them (TKT-35). **Priority:** P2 **Depends on:** TKT-102

This is the coexistence + contract slice: it moves a map from `draft` to `published`, lets a performance/slot reference a published map version, and extends the `performance.published` domain event so a seated slot conveys enough for inventory to provision seated pools later — **without building the seat claim itself** (that is TKT-80/TKT-4). The publish transition follows the ADR-018 row-lock-decide-emit-after-commit pattern. The event change follows ADR-017 (dispatch on schema before decoding `data`); inventory hard-switches on the event schema (ADR-014 warned of this), so the schema fork and inventory's tolerance of it are load-bearing — the plan must state whether inventory changes in lockstep or safely ignores the seated fork for now.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Publish transition on a seat map: `draft` → `published` decided under a row lock, event emitted only after commit, outbox column marked (ADR-018). A published map version is immutable (edits create a new version — the mechanics of the new version land in TKT-104).
- [ ] A performance can be created/published as **seated**, referencing a published map version; GA performances are unchanged and still publish through the existing path (M1 tests green). GA and seated coexist per venue.
- [ ] The `platform.catalog.performance.published` payload conveys the seated shape (e.g. seat/section counts or a map-version reference) under a **new schema fork** per ADR-017; the envelope and dispatch rules are honored. A contract test pins the new payload (ADR-009).
- [ ] Inventory's consumer is not broken by the seated event: either it provisions a seated pool in lockstep, or it safely ignores the seated fork (dispatch-on-schema), proven by a test. The seat-level claim itself remains out of scope (TKT-80).
- [ ] Publishing a seated performance is idempotent at the stream (deterministic event ID), matching the existing publish emission.

**Quality gates (every story):**
- `make check` green (lint + unit + integration + smoke; mirrors CI)
- Contract tests pass for any touched service boundary (ADR-009 drift check)
- New/changed public read endpoints declare an ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale
- New migrations run out-of-band via the service `migrate` subcommand (ADR-022) and build within the 30s startup budget with plain `CREATE INDEX` (ADR-020)
- Every owned entity is `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002)

Parent epic: TKT-3. Full lineage: docs/product/prd-v1.md §Capability map (TKT-3).

binding.rule: State-deriving catalog transitions decide under a row lock (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) and emit the domain event only after the store commits, marking the outbox column on success. The lock closes the check-then-act race against concurrent transitions.

Domain events use the `{id,type,occurred_at,schema,data}` envelope. Bump `schema` on consumer semantics, not parse compatibility; additive fields that all live consumers ignore may ride the current schema. A consumer dispatches on `schema` before decoding `data`.

Every admission-granting offer is a dated slot in one inventory machinery; slot attributes carry domain specifics (seated vs GA vs zoned, operating hours, closures) — the claim primitive does not fork.

governingAdrs.why: The map publish transition decides under FOR UPDATE and emits after commit — same shape as performance publish/archive.
The seated publish payload is a schema fork; a consumer must dispatch on schema before decoding data. The dangerous payload deserializes fine.
Inventory's consumer hard-switches on the published event's schema — a bump stops provisioning unless inventory moves in lockstep; decide and test which.
Seated is a slot attribute conveyed to inventory; the claim core still must not fork.
The changed event payload is a contract boundary — contract/drift tests must cover the new fork.

reference.summary: PRD v1 §Capability map — TKT-3 row is the source of truth for scope
TKT-3 epic — COS: authoring UI, versioning safe against sold inventory, GA+seated coexist
Catalog event envelope + publish emit-after-commit; PerformancePublishedData schema forks 2/3
Inventory consumer dispatches on (subject,schema) → Provision(poolID, capacity int32) — the seam the seated fork must not break
TKT-80 (US-017, TKT-4 epic) is the seat-level claim that consumes this contract — hard-blocked on TKT-3

#### ⚠️ Process-experiment waiver — this ticket runs **GATELESS** by explicit owner directive

The repo owner (running as PO) has **deliberately waived all four human gates** for this ticket as a process experiment, and asked that the waiver be recorded here so the board history shows it ran gateless. Gate replacements for this run:

- **Gate 1 (priority)** — already given: ticket is in Ready.
- **Gate 2 (plan approval)** — orchestrator stands in as judge after the cross-model plan critique. Per `ab-stages.md` §`plan` rule 6 (gate waived by owner directive ≠ `risk:low`): run **every** plan arm, critique all as `planReview`, self-select with stated reasons, and **disclose the arm mapping immediately** in the plan comment (anonymization is moot when the judge launched the arms). Open decisions resolved by: prefer the critique's recommended option; if none, the most reversible option. Every self-made decision + rationale recorded in `kind=plan-final`.
- **Gate 3 (review + merge)** — after the adversarial A/B ai-review converges (same triage / second-pass / churn-cap rules), orchestrator squash-merges the PR and deletes the branch. Review-guide posted on the PR first (the audit record).
- **Gate 4 (PO acceptance)** — orchestrator self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code, posts the validation note, closes with the full `kind=metrics` comment.

**Unchanged, non-negotiable:** `config.models` routing (no substitutions); cross-model review for plan *and* code; TDD with tests observed red first; `make check` green before every push and after merge; all marker comments at each stage; **no AI attribution** in commits/PRs.

**Not `risk:low`.** This ticket touches a domain-event schema fork and the inventory consumer contract (ADR-017/ADR-014) — exactly the class the plan gate exists to catch. The waiver substitutes the orchestrator-as-judge for the human gate; it does **not** downgrade the risk.

Cross-model invariant checked both pairs: planner arms ≠ main-agent, implementer (main-agent) ≠ aiReview arms. Clean.

Transitioning **Ready → Planning**, label `agent:planning`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft (A/B winner) — TKT-103 — drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex`

This is the **selected** plan draft from a 3-arm A/B (`plan` = [`kimi-k3:low@claudex`, `gpt-5.6-luna:high@claudex`, `gpt-5.6-luna:xhigh@claudex`]). The A/B tally, arm disclosure, my `planReview` (main-agent) verdicts, and the self-made Gate-2 decisions are in the `kind=plan-final` delta below. The draft is reproduced verbatim as the audit record:

---

## 1. Decision resolution

**(a) Schema number: 4.**  
Keep ungrouped GA at schema 2 and grouped festival slots at schema 3, as currently selected by `performancePublishedEnvelopeWithID` (`services/catalog/internal/events/events.go:209-237`). A seated payload changes the consumer-visible slot shape and adds required map-reference invariants, so ADR-017 requires a new `(type, schema)` variant rather than an additive field (`docs/adr/ADR-017-domain-event-schema-evolution.md:90-119`). Schema 4 carries the existing identifiers, `kind`, `re_entry`, and the exact published map reference (`seat_map_id` plus `seat_map_version`); it does not carry GA capacity or festival capacity fields.

**(b) Inventory changes in lockstep, but safely ignores the seated variant.**  
Inventory must recognize schema 4 before Catalog emits it. Leaving the current consumer unchanged would quarantine the event and latch readiness false (`services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:196-226`). Add a known schema-4 dispatch arm that validates the seated map reference, acknowledges the event, and performs no `Provision` call. This is the cheapest correct behavior because the current inventory pool is an anonymous quantity pool (`consumer.go:75-100`), while seat-level claiming is explicitly TKT-80 scope. It avoids exposing seated tickets through the GA quantity-claim path, consistent with ADR-005’s unified claim primitive (`docs/adr/ADR-005-unified-dated-slot-admission.md:25-28`).

Access must also recognize schema 4: it consumes the same publication subject and currently treats schema 4 as future skew (`services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go:28-38`, `:72-98`). Its schema-4 arm continues projecting `re_entry` and ignores seated-only fields.

**(c) Skew fixtures:**  
- Publication-schema future fixtures using `schema: 4` in `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer_test.go:215` move to `schema: 5`; schema 5 remains the unknown future publication variant.
- The publication registry/tripwire expectations in `consumer_test.go:416` and `:505`, plus `services/inventory/internal/consumer/offering_test.go:240`, move the publication maximum from 3 to 4.
- The archived-event fixture at `offering_test.go:120` remains `schema: 4`: schema numbers are scoped to `(type, schema)` under ADR-017 (`docs/adr/ADR-017-domain-event-schema-evolution.md:75-88`), and `performance.archived` still has known schemas only through 3. It must continue proving unknown archived-schema handling.
- Access’s current future-publication fixture at `services/access/internal/consumer/policy_test.go:112-130` moves from schema 4 to schema 5.

**(d) Seated pool provisioning:**  
No seated pool is provisioned in TKT-103. The schema-4 event conveys the exact published map/version reference so a later inventory implementation can provision from that immutable version. The schema-4 arm validates and safely acknowledges without creating a GA-style pool. TKT-80 owns the seat-level claim path.

**(e) COS-4 proof:**  
Add a handwritten schema-4 publication fixture to the inventory consumer tests asserting all of the following: schema 4 is dispatched as known; the event is acknowledged; no quarantine row is written; readiness remains true; and the inventory `Provision` seam is not called. Add the corresponding Access test asserting schema 4 still projects the re-entry policy. Preserve the existing handwritten, reshaped schema-5 fixture to prove dispatch happens before payload decoding, as required by ADR-017 (`docs/adr/ADR-017-domain-event-schema-evolution.md:175-199`).

**Transition concurrency resolution:**  
The ticket’s phrase “under a row lock” is looser than the governing ADR. ADR-018 explicitly says a monotonic `draft → published` transition remains correct with a plain conditional `UPDATE` and stays lock-free (`docs/adr/ADR-018-catalog-slot-transition-concurrency.md:62-66`). Seat-map publication is monotonic: no concurrent opposite transition can invalidate its event identity. Therefore implement it like `PublishPerformance` (`services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go:565-599`), not like `ArchivePerformance`: conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status='draft'`, commit, emit, then mark the event emitted.

**Seated representation:**  
Use the presence of a nullable `performances.seat_map_id` to distinguish seated from GA. Do not add a new `kind`; `kind` already describes the temporal slot shape (`services/catalog/internal/store/store.go:156-160`), and ADR-005 says seating is a slot attribute. `NULL` means unchanged GA behavior; non-NULL means a seated `performance` pinned to one published map row/version. Reject map references for grouped day slots and reject references whose organizer or venue differs from the performance.

## 2. DoD

- **COS-1:** Catalog can transition a draft seat map to published through a conditional monotonic store update; the committed row carries `published_at`, the event is emitted afterward, `event_emitted_at` is marked only after acknowledgement, and geometry writes remain draft-only.
- **COS-2:** `PerformanceCreate` accepts an optional published `seat_map_id`; the store validates published status, organizer, venue, and slot kind; non-null means seated, null preserves GA creation/publication and existing M1 behavior.
- **COS-3:** `performance.published` emits schema 4 for seated performances with the map/version reference; existing schema-2 and schema-3 payloads remain unchanged; the event contract test pins the new fork.
- **COS-4:** Inventory recognizes schema 4, safely acknowledges without provisioning or readiness failure; Access also recognizes it; tests prove no quarantine and no accidental GA pool.
- **COS-5:** Seated performance publication reuses `EventID(perf)` and the existing `event_emitted_at` owed-marker path, so retries use the same NATS message ID and stream-deduplicate.

## 3. Files

- `services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0010_publish_seat_maps.sql` — add seat-map publication metadata and the nullable performance-to-exact-map-version reference.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/migration_smoke_test.go` — advance the named rollback guard from `versionBeforeSeatMaps = 8` to the pre-0010 version, as required by the file’s explicit guard.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/store.go` — extend `SeatMap`, `Performance`, and `PerformanceInput`; add seat-map publication and emission-marker operations to the existing store port.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/postgres.go` — implement the conditional map publish transition, map event-marker update, map validation during performance creation, and performance projection/scanning of `seat_map_id`.
- `services/catalog/api/openapi.yaml` — add the seat-map publish operation and the optional performance map reference; document seated/GA validation and response shapes.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` — regenerate from the OpenAPI source; do not hand-edit.
- `web/backoffice/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts` — regenerate the catalog client types.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts` — regenerate the catalog client types.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/server.go` — add the generated publish handler, map response conversion, and seated performance input/output mapping; retain the existing emit-after-commit pattern at `:514-540`.
- `services/catalog/internal/events/events.go` — add the seat-map publication subject/publisher and deterministic map-event ID; add schema-4 seated selection and map-reference fields to the performance publication envelope while preserving schemas 2 and 3.
- `services/catalog/internal/events/events_test.go` — extend the existing `TestPerformancePublishedEnvelopeSchemas` table at `:14-67` with the seated schema-4 contract case and deterministic-ID assertions; add the seat-map publication envelope contract.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go` — extend the existing store/publisher fakes and performance publication tests for seated validation, retry, and GA regression.
- `services/catalog/internal/api/seatmap_test.go` — add publish success/idempotency/error cases beside the existing seat-map authoring tests.
- `services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_smoke_test.go` — add real-Postgres transition, post-publication immutability, marker, and organizer/venue validation coverage.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go` — add the schema-4 known arm and explicit no-op acknowledgement path; preserve envelope-first/schema-first dispatch.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer_test.go` — update publication maximum/tripwires, move future publication fixtures to schema 5, and test schema-4 acknowledgement without provisioning.
- `services/inventory/internal/consumer/offering_test.go` — keep archived schema 4 as the unknown archived variant and update only publication registry expectations if present.
- `services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go` — recognize publication schema 4 and project common policy fields.
- `services/access/internal/consumer/policy_test.go` — move the future publication fixture to schema 5 and add a seated schema-4 projection case.
- `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go` — extend the existing publication smoke flow at `:144-174` to assert seated schema 4 and retain the GA schema-2 regression.

No inventory migration is needed: the chosen COS-4 behavior does not create or persist a seated pool.

## 4. Test plan (TDD)

Write each case first and observe it fail before implementing the corresponding production change.

1. **Seat-map publication transition and immutability**
   - In `services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_smoke_test.go`, add cases proving a draft becomes published, repeated publication is idempotent, `published_at` remains stable, and section/row/seat writes no longer succeed after publication.
   - Assert the event marker is initially owed and is changed only by the explicit mark-emitted operation.
   - Add a concurrent publication case proving concurrent callers converge on one state and one deterministic event identity.

2. **Emit-after-commit and retry**
   - In `services/catalog/internal/api/seatmap_test.go` and `server_test.go`, add publisher-failure and retry cases analogous to the existing performance publication tests at `server_test.go:1113-1156`.
   - Assert failed publication leaves the marker owed, retry emits the same deterministic ID, and successful acknowledgement marks the row afterward.

3. **Seated performance validation**
   - In `services/catalog/internal/api/server_test.go`, add cases for:
     - published same-venue/same-organizer map succeeds;
     - draft map fails;
     - archived map fails;
     - missing map fails;
     - cross-organizer map fails;
     - cross-venue map fails;
     - map reference on a grouped/day slot fails.
   - Assert the response retains the pinned map ID/version.
   - Keep the existing valid GA case and assert a request with no map remains unchanged.

4. **Performance event contract**
   - In the existing `TestPerformancePublishedEnvelopeSchemas` table in `services/catalog/internal/events/events_test.go`, retain schema 2 for ordinary GA and schema 3 for grouped festival, then add schema 4 for a seated performance.
   - Decode the schema-4 data with a handwritten contract shape and assert the required map ID/version and common fields; assert GA/festival capacity fields are not used for the seated fork.
   - Add repeated-event assertions using `EventID(perf)` to prove the same seated publication produces the same envelope ID.
   - Add a seat-map publication envelope case asserting subject, schema, map ID/version, and deterministic ID.

5. **Inventory tolerance**
   - In `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer_test.go`, add a handwritten schema-4 payload with a valid map reference.
   - Assert the message is acknowledged, no quarantine call occurs, readiness remains true, and the provision store seam is untouched.
   - Add malformed known-schema-4 cases that terminate as poison rather than quarantine.
   - Move the existing unknown publication fixture from schema 4 to schema 5 and retain its quarantine/readiness assertions.
   - Preserve `TestEveryKnownSchemaHasAnArm` and `TestMaxKnownSchemaIsNotBehindTheArms`.

6. **Access tolerance**
   - In `services/access/internal/consumer/policy_test.go`, add schema-4 publication coverage proving re-entry projection still succeeds.
   - Move the current future-schema case to schema 5 and retain its parking/readiness assertions.

7. **GA regression and coexistence**
   - In `services/catalog/internal/store/seatmap_smoke_test.go`, retain the existing GA-capacity coexistence coverage.
   - In `smoke/catalog_publication_test.go`, publish both a seated performance referencing a map and an ordinary GA performance at the same venue; assert seated emits schema 4 and GA still emits schema 2 through the existing path.
   - Run the existing M1 performance publication tests without changing their fixtures.

8. **Contract and migration gates**
   - Add the new documented operation’s happy-path API coverage so catalog’s operation coverage test remains satisfied (`services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go:41-65`).
   - Assert responses through the existing OpenAPI-validating test harness (`server_test.go:965-1002`) and preserve served-spec identity coverage (`server_test.go:1393-1400`).
   - Run `make generate`, then `make check`.

## 5. Migration plan

Add `services/catalog/internal/store/migrations/0010_publish_seat_maps.sql` as an additive catalog migration.

Exact logical DDL:

```sql
ALTER TABLE seat_maps
    ADD COLUMN published_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    ADD COLUMN event_emitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

ALTER TABLE seat_maps
    ADD CONSTRAINT seat_maps_id_organizer_venue_key
    UNIQUE (id, organizer_id, venue_id);

ALTER TABLE performances
    ADD COLUMN seat_map_id UUID NULL;

ALTER TABLE performances
    ADD CONSTRAINT performances_seat_map_scope_fk
    FOREIGN KEY (seat_map_id, organizer_id, venue_id)
    REFERENCES seat_maps (id, organizer_id, venue_id);
```

Behavioral constraints:

- `seat_map_id IS NULL` is GA and leaves the existing performance path unchanged.
- `seat_map_id IS NOT NULL` is seated and must be validated as a published map for the same organizer and venue.
- The referenced `seat_maps.id` identifies the exact immutable version; no separate mutable “current map” lookup is allowed.
- Do not add a new index unless a new query filters by `seat_map_id`; no such read is required by this ticket. If a later query needs one, use plain `CREATE INDEX` under ADR-020, not `CONCURRENTLY`.
- Do not add an inventory migration because schema 4 is intentionally acknowledged without provisioning.

Compliance:

- The migration is embedded and run only by the catalog binary’s out-of-band `migrate` subcommand under ADR-022 (`docs/adr/ADR-022-out-of-band-service-migrations.md:99-121`).
- It must remain within the 30-second migration bound.
- It is organizer-scoped through the composite foreign key, consistent with ADR-002.
- Update the rollback guard in `migration_smoke_test.go` from the current pre-seat-map target of 8 to the pre-0010 target of 9; do not leave the named guard silently referring to the old latest migration.
- Keep the existing `performances.event_emitted_at` marker for performance publication (`0001_catalog_schema.sql` and `postgres.go:836`); add the analogous seat-map marker because the seat-map transition has its own event.

## 6. Risks & seams

- **Row-lock wording versus ADR-018:** do not implement `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` merely because the ticket uses that phrase. The transition is monotonic, so mirror `PublishPerformance`’s conditional update (`postgres.go:565-599`) and retain emit-after-commit. The seam is the new store publication test in `seatmap_smoke_test.go`.
- **Geometry race:** all existing geometry writes include `status='draft'` predicates (`postgres.go:1510-1575`); the publication update must also be conditional on draft so no child write that observes the committed published state can succeed. Cover concurrent publication/authoring in the real-Postgres smoke test.
- **Schema collision:** schema 4 becomes valid for `performance.published`, so publication future fixtures must move to 5. Do not move archived schema 4 because schemas are per event type. The seams are `consumer_test.go:215`, `offering_test.go:120`, and the registry tripwires.
- **Consumer hard switch:** inventory currently quarantines unknown publication schemas and latches readiness false (`consumer.go:196-226`). The schema-4 no-op arm must be implemented before Catalog emits schema 4; test with a handwritten reshaped future payload to preserve schema-first dispatch.
- **Second consumer:** Access also consumes `performance.published` and will become unready unless its maximum and dispatch arm are updated (`services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go:28-38`, `:72-98`).
- **Accidental GA provisioning:** do not route seated schema 4 through `provisionInput` cases 2 or 3. The schema-4 test must assert that the provision seam is not called.
- **Performance projection drift:** the canonical performance query currently derives `Capacity` from `venues.ga_capacity` (`postgres.go:618-656`). Add the map reference to every matching select/scan projection without changing the GA capacity behavior.
- **Generated contract drift:** OpenAPI is authoritative under ADR-009; regenerate `openapi_gen.go` and both TypeScript generated clients. `make check` must catch any mismatch.
- **Read-cache scope:** do not change existing public map-read caching in this ticket. The current geometry read uses the hours tier (`server.go:1087-1125`), while publication is a write and remains uncached. Draft-versus-published read exposure is a separate concern associated with TKT-107.
- **Map-version mechanics:** do not implement cloning, editing, or sold/held-seat remapping. The current map version is persisted in TKT-102, but new-version mechanics belong to TKT-104.

## 7. Out of scope

- Seat-level selection, reservation, claim, hold, or inventory seat identity behavior remains TKT-80/TKT-4 scope.
- Provisioning a usable seated inventory pool remains deferred; schema 4 only provides the immutable map/version reference and is safely acknowledged.
- Editing a published map by cloning it into a new version, version-family mechanics, and remapping performances remain TKT-104.
- Do not fork the inventory claim primitive or introduce a separate seated slot table; seating remains an attribute of the existing performance slot under ADR-005.
- Do not alter GA capacity, ordinary schema-2 publication, grouped schema-3 publication, or the existing M1 performance path.
- Do not change draft/published public-read exposure or cache policy beyond the new write endpoint; leave that follow-up to the existing read-scope work.

objective.note: Draft maps can't be offered; this publishes a map and lets a performance be offered as seated, and defines the catalog→inventory event contract that downstream seat claims (TKT-80) and buyer selection (TKT-35) consume — coexisting with GA.

scope.note: IN: seat-map draft→published transition (ADR-018 lock/emit-after-commit); a performance references a published map version; performance.published payload conveys the seated shape under a new schema fork (ADR-017); inventory consumer proven not to break (lockstep provision OR safe ignore). OUT: the seat-level claim itself (TKT-80/TKT-4); edit-after-publish safety (TKT-104); buyer UI (TKT-35).

uncertainties.note: Whether inventory provisions seated pools in lockstep or safely ignores the seated fork for now — an AC requires the plan to decide and test it. ADR-014 flags that inventory hard-switches on schema; dispatch-on-schema (ADR-017) is the tolerance mechanism. Resolvable in Planning; no product call.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-102 (needs a draft seat-map model to publish). Linked. Also the contract this ticket ships is consumed by TKT-80 (cross-epic, downstream — TKT-80 is blocked-by the epic).

approach.note: Map publish mirrors performance publish/archive: decide under FOR UPDATE, emit after commit, mark the outbox column (ADR-018). Seated payload rides a new schema fork on platform.catalog.performance.published; envelope + dispatch-on-schema per ADR-017; contract/drift tests per ADR-009. Claim core unchanged (ADR-005).

first_slice.note: Publish + seated-offer + the event fork + an inventory-tolerance test — the minimum that makes 'GA and seated coexist' true and the contract real, without building the claim.

success.note: COS: a map publishes under the lock/emit rule; a seated performance publishes referencing a map version while GA performances are untouched (M1 green); the published event carries the seated shape under a new schema, pinned by a contract test; inventory's consumer is proven safe against the new fork; publish is idempotent at the stream.

context_memo.note: Baked: ADR-018 (transition concurrency), ADR-017 (schema evolution/dispatch), ADR-014 (inventory schema hard-switch warning), ADR-005 (no fork), ADR-009 (contract). governingAdrs present.
